_meta.purpose: How a typical Indian lender decides a home loan. Only the LTV caps are law (RBI). Everything else is convention, differs by lender, and is shown as an editable assumption in the tool.

ltv.note: RBI: loan up to 90% of property value for loans up to ₹30 lakh, 80% for ₹30 to 75 lakh, 75% above ₹75 lakh. Stamp duty, registration and other charges are excluded from 'value' and cannot be financed. The band is decided by the loan amount, not the property price.

foir.basis_note: Most sanctioning teams work from net monthly take-home on the salary slip; some lender calculators quote the same percentages against gross. Switch the basis to see the difference.
foir.note: Total EMIs including the new loan as a share of monthly income. Rises with income because living costs are a smaller share. Bank-specific figures quoted publicly: HDFC about 48-60%, ICICI 45-50%, Bank of Maharashtra 40-50%.

income_haircuts.note: Bonus and variable pay are usually counted at half of a two-year average or ignored; rental income at 70-75%; a co-applicant's income in full.

obligations.note: Every existing EMI counts in full; revolving credit-card balances are usually taken at 5% of the outstanding.

credit_score.note: No bank publishes a hard floor; 700+ is the practical minimum and 750+ gets the best rate. SBI prices explicitly by score. Below about 650 expect a refusal regardless of income.

age.lender_variants: SBI allows the loan to run to age 70 for both; HDFC 65 for salaried and 70 for self-employed; many PSU banks use retirement age (60) for salaried.

rate.range_note: Home loan rates in September 2026 run from about 7.25% (top score, large PSU bank) to 8.45% for salaried borrowers; the tool adds the score premium to whatever base you type.
